rubrics.justification: The response accurately identifies an expanded blastocyst with a prominent left-sided ICM and relatively loose/scant TE, broadly matching a 3AB image. Minor overstatements include claiming circumferentially clear TE discontinuity details and absence of collapse/debris significance beyond what can be confidently inferred from a single image.

It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, male-factor context, endometrial thickness, first-cycle status, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis, showing how each modifies expected outcome.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear progression from morphology and patient factors to prognosis and recommendations. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments and an arguably imprecise statement about euploid rates at age 36.

The assessment is largely consistent with Gardner grading and standard IVF practice, including single good-quality blastocyst transfer considerations and lifestyle counseling. Small deviations include suggesting ERA relatively early and discussing assisted hatching despite limited indication here.

Recommendations are specific and practical, covering immediate transfer management, luteal support considerations, counseling on alcohol and weight, cryopreservation, and contingency planning for future cycles.
